The display device includes a substrate having a display region and a peripheral region surrounding or adjacent to the display region. Display structures, such as light-emitting elements, pixel circuits, electrodes, and related functional layers, are disposed in the display region of the substrate.

A first block member is arranged in the peripheral region of the substrate. The first block member is positioned so as to surround the display structures, thereby helping to define or protect the area in which the display structures are located. The first block member may function as a barrier or dam structure for controlling the spread of subsequently formed layers.

A second block member is also disposed in the peripheral region. The second block member is spaced apart from the first block member and surrounds the first block member. The second block member has a height greater than that of the first block member. Because of this increased height and its outer position, the second block member can provide an additional barrier function, improving containment of encapsulation materials and enhancing protection against external contaminants such as moisture or oxygen.

A first encapsulation layer is formed over the substrate. The first encapsulation layer covers the display structures, the first block member, and the second block member. In this manner, the first encapsulation layer provides a continuous protective covering over both the active display components and the surrounding block members.

A second encapsulation layer is formed over the first encapsulation layer. The second encapsulation layer overlaps at least a portion of the first block member in the depth dimension, for example in a direction perpendicular to the substrate. This arrangement can improve the sealing performance of the encapsulation structure and help prevent moisture or other contaminants from reaching the display structures.
outputs.L4:
A display device and a method for manufacturing the display device are provided. The display device includes a substrate having a display region in which image-producing elements are formed and a peripheral region surrounding the display region. A plurality of display structures, such as light-emitting elements, thin-film transistors, electrodes, insulating layers, and related wiring, may be disposed in the display region of the substrate.

In the peripheral region, block members are arranged around the display region to assist in sealing and protecting the display structures. The block members may include an inner block member and an outer block member positioned outside the inner block member. These block members may have different heights. In particular, the outer block member may be formed to have a greater height than the inner block member. By providing the outer block member with a larger height, the structure can more effectively restrict the spread of encapsulation material and provide an improved barrier against external moisture, oxygen, dust, and other contaminants.

An encapsulation structure is formed over the display region and at least a portion of the peripheral region. The encapsulation structure may include one or more encapsulation layers, such as inorganic encapsulation layers, organic encapsulation layers, or a multilayer combination thereof. At least one encapsulation layer may extend over the display structures and overlap the block members arranged in the peripheral region. The encapsulation layer may cover the inner block member and may further extend toward or onto the taller outer block member. In some configurations, the encapsulation structure overlaps both the inner block member and the outer block member, thereby increasing the effective sealing path around the display region.

The difference in height between the block members helps control the deposition and flow of encapsulation materials during manufacturing. For example, when an organic encapsulation material is applied, the inner block member may limit lateral spreading of the material, while the taller outer block member may serve as an additional barrier. This arrangement improves the uniformity and reliability of the encapsulation structure and reduces the likelihood that moisture or oxygen will penetrate into the display region through the peripheral area.

A method of manufacturing the display device may include preparing the substrate having the display region and the peripheral region, forming the display structures in the display region, forming the block members in the peripheral region around the display region, and forming the encapsulation structure over the display structures and the block members. The block members may be formed by patterning one or more insulating or organic layers so that the outer block member has a height greater than that of the inner block member. The encapsulation layers may then be deposited or coated to cover the display region and overlap at least part of the peripheral sealing structure.

Through this configuration, the display device can obtain enhanced sealing performance and improved protection of the display elements. The taller outer block member, together with the overlapping encapsulation layers, creates a more robust barrier structure around the display region. As a result, penetration of external moisture and oxygen can be suppressed, damage to the display structures can be reduced, and the operational lifetime and reliability of the display device can be improved.
outputs.L5:
A display device is an electronic output device that presents visual information to users. It allows people to view text, images, videos, graphics, and interactive content generated by a computer, smartphone, television, or other digital system. Display devices are essential in modern technology because they make digital information easy to see, understand, and use.

Common examples of display devices include computer monitors, television screens, smartphone displays, tablet screens, projectors, and digital signage. These devices use different technologies to produce images. For example, LCD displays use liquid crystals and backlighting, while OLED displays use organic light-emitting diodes that can produce bright colors and deep blacks. LED screens are also widely used because they are energy-efficient and provide clear, vivid images.

The quality of a display device is often measured by features such as screen size, resolution, brightness, refresh rate, color accuracy, and viewing angle. A higher resolution, such as Full HD, 4K, or 8K, means that the screen can show more detail. A higher refresh rate makes motion appear smoother, which is especially useful for gaming, sports, and video editing.

Display devices are used in many areas of daily life. In education, they help teachers present lessons and students access digital learning materials. In business, they support presentations, video meetings, and data analysis. In entertainment, they provide access to movies, games, and online content. In public places, display devices are used for advertising, information boards, transportation schedules, and safety messages.

Overall, a display device is an important part of digital communication. It connects users with information in a visual way and plays a major role in work, learning, entertainment, and everyday activities.

In one aspect, an organic light-emitting diode (OLED) display device is provided. The OLED display device includes a substrate including a display region and a peripheral region surrounding the display region, a plurality of OLED elements disposed in the display region, and an encapsulation structure disposed over the plurality of OLED elements. A first block member is disposed in the peripheral region so as to surround the display region, and a second block member is disposed outside the first block member and also surrounds the display region. The encapsulation structure includes a multilayer encapsulation layer having at least one inorganic encapsulation layer and at least one organic encapsulation layer. The first and second block members are configured to restrict lateral flow of the organic encapsulation layer during formation of the multilayer encapsulation layer and to improve a sealing characteristic of the display region.

In one implementation, the first block member is positioned closer to the display region than the second block member, and the organic encapsulation layer is disposed within an area bounded by at least one of the first block member and the second block member. The inorganic encapsulation layer may extend over the first block member and toward or over the second block member to form a moisture and oxygen barrier. The first and second block members may have different heights, widths, materials, or cross-sectional profiles to control spreading of an organic encapsulation material and to enhance adhesion between encapsulation layers and the substrate.

In another aspect, a method of manufacturing an OLED display device is provided. The method includes forming a plurality of OLED elements in a display region of a substrate, forming a first block member in a peripheral region of the substrate to surround the display region, forming a second block member outside the first block member to surround the display region, and forming a multilayer encapsulation layer over the plurality of OLED elements. Forming the multilayer encapsulation layer includes forming a first inorganic encapsulation layer over the plurality of OLED elements, depositing an organic encapsulation material over the first inorganic encapsulation layer such that lateral spreading of the organic encapsulation material is limited by at least one of the first and second block members, curing the organic encapsulation material to form an organic encapsulation layer, and forming a second inorganic encapsulation layer over the organic encapsulation layer. The first and second block members thereby define a confinement structure for the organic encapsulation layer and contribute to preventing penetration of moisture or oxygen into the display region.

## Patent Disclosure: Display Device Encapsulation Structure

### Title  
Display Device Having Multi-Height Peripheral Blocking Walls and Encapsulation Layers

### Abstract  
A display device includes a substrate, a display region disposed on the substrate, and a peripheral blocking structure surrounding the display region. The peripheral blocking structure includes a first blocking wall and a second blocking wall, wherein the first blocking wall is positioned closer to the display region and has a height lower than that of the second blocking wall. A first encapsulation layer is disposed over the display region and extends to cover both the first blocking wall and the second blocking wall. A second encapsulation layer is disposed on the first encapsulation layer and extends outwardly to cover at least a portion of the first blocking wall. The structure improves encapsulation reliability while controlling overflow of encapsulation material.

### Technical Field  
The disclosure relates to display devices, and more particularly to encapsulation structures for organic light-emitting diode displays, micro-LED displays, or other moisture-sensitive display devices.

### Summary  
A display device is provided including a substrate having a display area and a peripheral area surrounding the display area. A plurality of blocking walls is arranged in the peripheral area. The plurality of blocking walls includes a first blocking wall adjacent to the display area and a second blocking wall disposed outward of the first blocking wall. The first blocking wall has a height lower than a height of the second blocking wall. A first encapsulation layer covers the display area and extends over the first and second blocking walls. A second encapsulation layer is formed over the first encapsulation layer and extends over at least part of an inner side or upper portion of the first blocking wall.  

The lower first blocking wall facilitates gradual spreading of the second encapsulation material, while the higher second blocking wall provides enhanced blocking against lateral overflow and moisture ingress.

### Example Claim  
1. A display device comprising:  
   a substrate comprising a display area and a peripheral area surrounding the display area;  
   a first blocking wall disposed in the peripheral area adjacent to the display area;  
   a second blocking wall disposed in the peripheral area outside the first blocking wall, wherein a height of the first blocking wall is lower than a height of the second blocking wall;  
   a first encapsulation layer covering the display area, the first blocking wall, and the second blocking wall; and  
   a second encapsulation layer disposed on the first encapsulation layer and extending over at least a portion of the first blocking wall.

### Advantageous Effects  
The disclosed structure improves encapsulation coverage, reduces risk of encapsulation overflow, and enhances resistance to moisture and oxygen penetration at the periphery of the display device.
counterfactuals.label: cf_4

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a technical abstract for a patent application about preventing encapsulation overflow in a display device using spaced block members in the peripheral region with different heights.
counterfactuals.output: A display device includes a substrate having a display region and a peripheral region surrounding at least a portion of the display region, a display element disposed in the display region, and an encapsulation structure covering the display element. The peripheral region includes a plurality of block members spaced apart from one another along an encapsulation boundary. The plurality of block members include at least a first block member having a first height and a second block member having a second height different from the first height. During formation of the encapsulation structure, the spaced block members interrupt, slow, or redirect flow of an encapsulation material in the peripheral region, while the height difference between adjacent or neighboring block members provides staged flow resistance and accommodates variations in coating volume, surface tension, and process tolerance. Accordingly, overflow of the encapsulation material beyond a desired encapsulation area is suppressed without requiring a continuous dam structure, thereby improving encapsulation reliability, reducing defects in a bezel or pad region, and enabling a narrow peripheral area in the display device.
